issues.issue: Did the officer unreasonably fail to apply the published guidelines and transitional provisions that allegedly allow LCP permanent residence after the program ended?
issues.applicant_position: Guidelines allow LCP applications with two years' experience and an LMIA filed by 2014; the officer overlooked them and the transitional provisions.
issues.respondent_position: Repealed s.113(1)(c) still applied after abolition and requires an LCP work permit; the guidelines do not change that.
issues.result_quote: it was reasonable for the Immigration Officer to conclude Ms. Rimando did not qualify for permanent residence under the Live-In Caregiver Class.

issues.issue: Did Ms. Rimando have to hold an LCP work permit when she applied for permanent residence, under s.113(1)(c)?
issues.applicant_position: She was not required to hold an LCP permit when applying, per the guidelines and transitional provisions.
issues.respondent_position: Paragraph 113(1)(c) required holding an LCP work permit at application; she did not hold one then.
issues.result_quote: paragraph 113(1)(c) of the pre 2017 Regulations unequivocally confirms this requirement

issues.issue: Did a legitimate expectation of permanent residence arise from the partial reading of the guidelines?
issues.applicant_position: The published guidelines created a legitimate and reasonable expectation that she would qualify for permanent residence.
issues.respondent_position: No legitimate expectation can arise contrary to law; the transitional regulatory requirements continue to apply.
issues.result_quote: no legitimate expectation can arise that is contrary to law
